sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg – Germany Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTA)
Luxembourg – United States DTA (US-Luxembourg Income Tax Treaty)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 27 June 2018 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and amending the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; CSSF Regulation 12-02; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/815; Grand-Ducal implementing regulations on the RBE.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (fully public access restricted; access granted to national supervisory authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit, and AML/CFT obliged entities during customer due diligence, plus legitimate-interest access under Article 6 of the Law of 27 June 2018)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authentic Articles of Association / Notarial Deed of Constitution for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised in Luxembourg; no Hague Apostille required where executed by a Luxembourg notary, but foreign-language translations must be certified as conforming

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Corporate Authorisation of each corporate foreign shareholder / general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original competent corporate registry / trade registrar of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued in an Apostille Convention state; otherwise full Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised and certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or entity authorised to certify identity documents in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille as required by Luxembourg law for non-EU documents, with sworn translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all UBOs, directors, and the general partner/manager using EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List and US watchlists, as well as the Luxembourg domestic sanctions tracker (Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, Directorate of Financial Sanctions). PEP status must be determined applying FATF, and CSSF/AML compulsory monitoring shall flag any adverse media, politically exposed person status, and restrictive measures screening before registration and throughout the CDD file lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online filing portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be expressed in Latin script; French, German, English, or Luxembourgish formations are accepted. The legal form designator 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' must be included. The name must comply with the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, avoid confusion with existing protected B2B/B2C brands, and respect Luxembourg and EU rules concerning deceptive names. Any non-Latin transliteration requires certified alignment with the RCS registered spelling.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: naming tokens implying sovereign or governmental authority or public-law functions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days from the RCS acceptance. Extension is generally not granted by the registry. Upon rejection by the RCS, the applicant may file a reasoned appeal to the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice within one month of the rejection notice. Where the refusal concerns a matter of commercial registry interpretation, the applicant may alternatively file a petition with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within two months of the refusal, supported by counsel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are accepted only for initial form registration purposes, provided the SCSp maintains a verifiable registered address in Luxembourg and local substance is established within the first operational month. For marine bunkering and lubricant replenishment, the undertaking must maintain a local compliance contact, board meeting venue, accounts, and bank account within Luxembourg; virtual-office-only structures will fail the substance assessment under Luxembourg tax and AML rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-High — estimated 40% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and cross-border fuel/trading exposure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and name reservation fee in the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for name check and pre-reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of constitution (authentic act) for an SCSp with no minimum capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary appointed by applicant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff on notary's scale of fees, dependent upon volume and complexity; standard benchmark for SCSp formation without capital distribution

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration filing with the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and publication in the Official Electronic Bulletin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS filing and electronic publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure and verification filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RBE filing tariff and data maintenance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and Consular Legalization of foreign corporate registry documents, passports, and UBO identity bundles (estimated 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate in the origin jurisdiction plus competent foreign authentication authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing apostille and consular legalization tariffs per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Anti-Money-Laundering / KYC UBO and PEP screening using sanitised international databases and sanctions scan
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Screening provider and instructed Luxembourg law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence screening of a cross-border bunkering legal entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal advisory on SCSp formation, name clearance appeals, and stage-1 compliance opinion for ISIC 5222 marine bunkering
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm retained by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for Luxembourg corporate counsel; flat fee inclusive of UBO structuring and regulatory risk review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 1-1, 13-1 to 13-19 (SCSp regime introduced by Law of 23 July 2016); Grand-Ducal Regulations on RCS registration and publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated via electronic filing portal (guichet.lu / lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement / Articles of Association (Contrat de société or Acte constitutif) for a Société en Commandite Spéciale, executed either by notarial deed or by private writing with certified signatures.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for SCSp; no escrow account required. Capital must be freely determined by the partnership agreement, and each partner's contribution must be fully subscribed as stipulated. General partner liability is unlimited; limited partners' liability is capped at their contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural meeting of the SCSp held this day at the registered office, the general partner, acting as management, resolved: (1) to confirm the subscription of partnership interests by the initial partners as recorded in the partnership agreement; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address] in Luxembourg; (3) to appoint [Name] as manager (gérant) with sole signature authority for, inter alia, opening bank accounts and executing bunkering supply contracts; (4) to initiate RCS registration and obtain all sectoral permits for ship refueling operations; (5) to authorize the manager to file all statutory declarations and represent the partnership before tax and regulatory authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify name availability and reserve corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS name reservation service via lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the RCS portal to confirm that the proposed SCSp name and any trade name do not conflict with existing legal entities or trademarks. File an online reservation request including the desired name, the entity type (SCSp), and applicant credentials. The reservation is valid for two months and is mandatory before notarization if the deed will use the reserved name.
required_dossiers: Application form for name reservation
Identity document and power of attorney of the applicant
Non-conflicting name search result from RCS database
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit an amended application with a variation (e.g., adding distinguishing element) or provide trademark coexistence consent from the prior owner; appeal within one month to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg if refusal persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if notarial deed) or certified private deed via Luxembourg lawyer; RCS registry for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement in accordance with mandatory Luxembourg law, including partners' roles (general and limited), capital contributions, profit sharing, management authority, transfer restrictions, and succession provisions. Execute before a Luxembourg notary (recommended to facilitate registration) or by private deed with certified signatures. Arrange for legalization of foreign signatures and apostille where partners are non-residents.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Certified copies of passports of all partners
Proof of address for each partner
Bank references or source-of-funds declarations for AML compliance
Power of attorney for legal counsel (if applicable)
Name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting errors or missing mandatory clauses by executing an amendment rectificative (amendment rectification deed); if notary blocks due to suspect corporate purpose, refine the purpose clause to exclude unlicensed bunkering activities and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open bank account and deposit initial contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., bank) or EEA-branch credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a bank and submit the notarized partnership agreement, RCS name confirmation, KYC/AML documentation of partners, and the intended business profile (marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment). Transfer the subscribed capital (if any) into a segregated client account and obtain an account deposit confirmation. If no capital is paid immediately, the partnership must record a declaration of unpaid contributions.
required_dossiers: Notarized partnership agreement
RCS name reservation certificate
AML/KYC forms for all partners and beneficial owners
Business plan and projected turnover for sulfur emission compliance
Proof of physical registered office or intention to establish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML information, provide a detailed source-of-funds ledger and references from existing settlement banks; if declined, use a second bank or obtain a letter of no-objection from the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application electronically via the RCS e-filing portal, attaching the signed partnership agreement, notarized deed if to be published, extract of the bank account blocked confirmation (if capital paid up), identification of registered office, and the manager's consent/identity. Pay the statutory filing fee and applicable publication fees online. The filing must be made within one month of deed execution.
required_dossiers: Application form (formulaire C) signed by authorized person
Partnership agreement / notarial deed
Bank certificate of deposit (if capital contributed)
Consent of manager(s) to appointment
Declaration of registered office address
Extract of criminal record for managers (less than 2 months old)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (e.g., missing annexes), address the defect within 15 days by refiling corrected documents; for formal errors, obtain a rectification order from the notary or court; await express approval before commencing business requiring RCS identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish mandatory legal notice in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Official Journal (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg – RESA electronic platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registrar automatically publishes a statutory excerpt (identification, registered office, object, legal representatives) in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA). Verify publication and retain proof for counterparties and licensing applications. If publication is not automatic (private deed case), separately file a copy of the deed with the RESA.
required_dossiers: RCS registration confirmation
Copy of the filed partnership agreement
Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of any published inaccuracies by submitting a request rectificative to the RCS with supporting documents; no litigation anticipated unless a third party has relied on erroneous publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, social security and statistical identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS), Statec for business register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file a single standardized registration form (Formulaire de constitution/entreprise) through the guichet GOC (gestionnaire officiel de clientèle) or through MyGuichet to obtain: (a) Luxembourg VAT number (due to bunkering supplies deemed supply of goods taxable in Luxembourg unless B2B reverse-charge or export rules apply); (b) corporate/partnership tax file and employer registration; (c) social security account for any salaried staff. Provide RCS extract and partnership agreement; select appropriate NACE/ISIC codes (5222) and indicate the intention to supply marine fuel in Luxembourg territory and on inland waterways.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (dated within 15 days)
Partnership agreement
For VAT: cross-border transaction declarations if any EU vessel supplies
Identification of the tax representative (if non-resident general partner)
Proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, file a late-registration notification with the AEDT and request expedited processing based on intended vessel departure dates; any penalties or interest may be waived by showing reasonable cause (force majeure or administrative delay).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Energy (Ministère de l'Énergie) and Ministry of the Economy, in conjunction with the Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploiter une installation de stockage et de distribution de carburants (Operating permit for fuel storage and distribution installation, including ship bunkering and refueling facilities).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency - Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA required for fuel storage installations with capacity exceeding 1,000 tonnes; medium registration for smaller storage tanks (Class 1A under Law of 15 June 2018 on environmental impact assessment); lower-tier assessment via notification for facilities below 100 tonnes integrated into an existing port infrastructure.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet water protection thresholds: pH 6.5–8.5, total hydrocarbons < 5 mg/L, BOD5 < 25 mg/L, COD < 125 mg/L, suspended solids < 30 mg/L; VOCs emissions from storage tanks limited to 10,000 mg/Nm³ for automated loading, 35,000 mg/Nm³ for manual; all fuel transfer areas require sealed containment basins and oil trap separators with 100% retention of accidental spillage; compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions) and Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 April 2018 on environmental permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) based on a fire-fighting plan, detection and alarm systems, fire-escape routing, and water supply points; structural load clearance certificate from the Administration des bâtiments publics (for permanent installations) and inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for workplace safety, including explosion-proof equipment (ATEX zones), confined-space entry procedures, and operator training records. The bunkering vessel and any mobile refueling equipment must receive a separate certificate of conformity from the Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics (inland navigation authorization under Luxembourg inland waterway regulations).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes; Luxembourg Indirect Tax Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT; Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (Administration des douanes et accises) for customs and export formalities. Primary taxpayer portal: MyGuichet.lu (business eSpace) and the RCS/RBE single registration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity obtaining a Luxembourg tax identity must first complete RCS registration (single RBE filing) to obtain the Luxembourg business registration number (matricule). The ACD automatically allocates the national income tax identification number based on the RCS matricule. For VAT purposes, the AEDT requires separate registration via Form 640 before supplies are made; non-established foreign operators must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative unless an EU-established entity can register directly. Direct tax ID is mandatory for any permanent establishment, partnership, or taxable activity; VAT ID follows the standard LU + 12-digit format.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Default: SCSp is fiscally transparent; all income, gains, deductions, and credits flow through to partners. Under Article 174bis LIR, the SCSp may elect optional full taxation as a corporation if it is a commercial partnership, maintains corporate-style accounts, and all partners are either Luxembourg residents or taxable through a Luxembourg PE, thereby becoming entity-level taxed and enabling the application of double tax treaty benefits. Other elections include the EU fiscal unity regime (integration fiscale) for direct tax under Article 164bis LIR and VAT group election under Article 61ter LVT, plus ATAD hybrid-mismatch filing elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Luxembourg VAT / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small business exemption for Luxembourg-established entities); non-established foreign suppliers performing taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register for VAT from the first euro of turnover, with no threshold exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing clearance currently applies to Luxembourg B2B transactions. Business-to-government e-invoicing must be issued in Peppol-BIS format on the PEPPOL network for public procurement invoicing. VAT returns and recapitulative statements (Intrastat, EU sales lists) must be filed electronically through MyGuichet/ACD-AEDT e-filing modules. For marine bunkering supplies, customs export clearances are processed via Luxembourg's Customs EDP/ECS system (part of EU Customs Decision Management system).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Marine fuel supplies (bunkers) delivered as stores provisioning to vessels engaged in international traffic qualify for VAT zero-rating (0%) under Luxembourg VAT law implementing EU VAT Directive Article 148; the zero-rated treatment covers supplies of fuel and lubricants for commercial ships operating on international voyages, including transport to/from third countries. The eligibility requires the vessel to be an eligible seagoing or inland-waterway vessel engaged in international navigation, and the bunker supply must be physically delivered at the Luxembourg port or as ship stores for the voyage. Re-supply during a voyage carrying passengers or goods between Luxembourg and another EU/third-country port also qualifies; supplies to yachts or private vessels do not qualify unless used for chartering to third parties with an economic activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (sea waybill, barge/ship manifests)
Inward Remittance Certificate or commercial bank wire/SWIFT proof of payment from the shipowner/operator
Bunker delivery receipt / marine fuel delivery note (MFDN) endorsed by the vessel's bunkering officer
Ship's logbook extract proving the international voyage
Charter party agreement or fixture note showing third-country destination
IMO number and vessel registration certificate
Declaration by the buyer/operator of the vessel's international-trade status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs exercise stringent ex-post audit review of export zero-rating claims for bunker supplies. If the zero-rating is not substantiated with the full documentation bundle within the statutory audit timeline, the VAT is retrospectively clawed back with default interest from the due date. Penalties for negligent or intentional VAT evasion range from 10% to 100% of the tax evaded; criminal prosecution can result in fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for repeat fraud. Under Luxembourg tax limitation rules, assessments may be reopened up to five years (ordinary cases), extended to ten years for fraud. Export zero-rating is strictly denied for supplies to fishing vessels, pleasure craft, or inland vessels used exclusively within domestic waterways absent an international-trade test.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); monetary policy and foreign exchange competences are exercised jointly with the European Central Bank (ECB) under the Eurosystem. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign exchange administration; AML/CFT and financial-sector integrity supervision is carried out by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) over credit institutions and e-money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full liberalisation of capital and current account transactions applies by virtue of EU law (Articles 63-66 TFEU); Luxembourg imposes no exchange-control authorisation for bunker fuel import/export payments, SCSp profit distributions, or investor capital repatriation. The euro is fully convertible and USD/EUR/other-currency settlement is unrestricted. Remittance hurdles are limited to (i) CSSF/BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, (ii) AML verification of beneficial owners under the Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), and (iii) FATCA/CRS and Luxembourg withholding tax compliance on qualifying interest and dividend payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Luxembourg; bunkering receivables may remain denominated in USD or any freely convertible currency without a repatriation deadline. The only functional conversion arises for Luxembourg statutory annual accounts, which must be kept in EUR (or a documented functional currency) for Commercial Code and tax reporting purposes; this is an accounting translation obligation, not a surrender obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational EUR/USD Current Account; Trade Finance and Standby LC Account
Operational Account; Escrow Collateral Account for SBLC
Operational Settlement Account; Commercial Letter of Credit Facility
Operational Account; Trade Finance and FX Hedging Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as the primary treasury rail and MEDIUM only as a satellite operational account. A Luxembourg CSSF-licensed e-money institution (fully authorised under the E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC) can legally host SCSp funds and provide IBANs, but large bunkering settlements (typically EUR 0.5M-10M per stem) require Tier 1 bank-grade SWIFT correspondent access and vessel-counterparty sanctions screening, which most offshore and UK-based digital EMIs cannot support. A passported EEA EMI may handle low-value port expenses such as pilotage, agency fees, and crew wages, but must not receive or disburse physical bunker fuel payments without a full commodity-trade AML programme.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg statute (Law of 12 November 2004) does not impose an unconditional in-person appearance, but CSSF Regulation 12-02 and bank-level AML policies require robust identification of all SCSp beneficial owners. In practice, banks mandate either (i) a face-to-face interview of at least one managing director (gérant) at the Luxembourg branch or (ii) a fully remote opening supported by a video-conference KYC with a Luxembourg notary or law-firm attestation, original notarised passports, EU banking references, and a completed RBE filing for the SCSp. For non-EU resident UBOs, the minimum accepted standard is video KYC with a Luxembourg-regulated lawyer or notary, supported by an apostilled identity and ownership bundle; no bank will open a bunkering treasury account on documents alone without senior compliance sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the SCSp's transparent partnership structure with silent partners and unidentified principals prevents the bank from determining the true economic owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract; notarised partnership agreement with a full capital table; side letters disclosing all economic beneficiaries; organisational chart of every entity holding 25% or more; signed source-of-wealth declarations and passport copies of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and vessel flag risk: payments are routed for vessels with flags of convenience or ports of call in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Russia-affiliated shipping, Venezuela, Iran, North Korea).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial sanctions-screening output from Dow Jones or LexisNexis for all counterparties; vessel IMO number with registry extract; charterparty and Bill of Lading; negative-media check results from the bank; written confirmation that the physical supplier holds a valid supply licence and that the receiving vessel is not on the OFAC, EU, or UN consolidated sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or opaque physical supply flows: inability to evidence actual delivery and marine-fuel quantity/quality, creating a trade-based money-laundering red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional dossier: signed commercial contract; bunker delivery note (BDN) with quantity and grade; master's receipt and hold survey; quantity surveyor certificate (e.g., SGS, Intertek, Lloyd's Register); invoice reconciliation to the MT103; voyage/charter order; and the supplier's corporate bank statement confirming same-fund settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent vehicle misuse: the bank suspects the SCSp is a FATCA/CRS non-reporting shell used to conceal taxable profit from bunkering trading.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cross-border tax memo from a Big-4 firm confirming SCSp pass-through treatment; executed CRS/FATCA self-certifications and W-8IMY with GIIN wherever relevant; Luxembourg substance file including registered office, local bank appointment, and management meeting minutes; draft annual accounts proving genuine economic activity in Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound subscription capital is routed under EU free-movement-of-capital rules with no exchange-control approval. EUR injections use SEPA Credit Transfer on TARGET2 with purpose code EQUI (equity investment); USD and other-currency injections use SWIFT MT103 with a remittance reference describing the equity subscription and the BCL balance-of-payments statistical classification. Each payment must originate from the exact investor account named in the subscription agreement; third-party funding and cash deposits are prohibited. The receiving bank books the funds to a dedicated capital escrow account, performs wire verification against a signed subscription form, and compiles a UBO/source-of-wealth file before converting the funds to operational cash. USD-EUR conversion is executed as an onboarding spot FX trade, with monthly BoP statistical reporting to the BCL.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All bunker fuel settlements execute via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for open-account stems and via MT700 documentary letters of credit or MT760 standby letters of credit for secured stems. The clearing rail requires full three-way matching of the commercial invoice, the BDN, and the master's receipt before release; USD payments settle through a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank's New York correspondent via CHIPS or Fedwire, and EUR payments settle through TARGET2/SEPA. SBLCs issued by the SCSp's bank in favour of physical suppliers must contain a clean, on-demand payment undertaking governed by Luxembourg law; the issuance is recorded as a commitment in the SCSp's annual accounts, requiring an authorised credit line and demonstrable economic substance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards (plain vanilla) with a CSSF-licensed bank under the ISDA 1998 FX definitions
EUR/USD FX options (European-style calls, puts, collars, and risk reversals) for hedging volatile USD bunker payables
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to match long-term instalments or term-loan repayments of the SCSp
FX swaps (tom-next and spot-next) for short-term funding and liquidity conversion

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for restricted currencies with no deliverable market (e.g., certain Asian or petro-state exotic FX pairs); EUR/USD NDFs are not permissible because the EUR/USD market is fully convertible and deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Data Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des données)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar year: due 31 March (confirmation window runs from 1 January to 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,000; persistent failure to confirm may trigger judicial strike-off after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 March following the accounting year; electronic filing automatically extends the deadline to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to 10% of the tax due (minimum EUR 50); late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; criminal penalties for willful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Record Confirmation embedded in RCS Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, synchronized with the RCS data-confirmation campaign
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 per individual and administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 for the entity; publication of sanction possible

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit becomes mandatory when the SCSp exceeds any two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years: (i) average balance sheet total above EUR 20 million; (ii) annual net turnover above EUR 40 million; (iii) average employment headcount above 250. Below these thresholds the SCSp is generally exempt from appointing an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Lux GAAP) pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002; IFRS is permitted for the consolidated financial statements and may be applied at entity level when the SCSp participates in a syndicated listed credit structure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner of the SCSp must maintain an internal, up-to-date register of ultimate beneficial owners. Although Luxembourg law does not require a separate annual UBO filing, the annual RCS confirmation process requires a positive declaration confirming continued accuracy of all beneficial-owner data previously filed. Any change in partnership interests, control, or UBO status arising during the calendar year must be reported to the RCS within 30 calendar days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (limited partners and general partner)
Register of directors of the general partner entity and any delegated managers
Minute book comprising minutes of partners' meetings and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 850 (typically EUR 300 - EUR 700 per annum)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a focused partnership audit; not applicable if the SCSp remains below the compulsory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no CIT or municipal business tax is assessed at the partnership level. Luxembourg-resident corporate partners are taxed on their allocated profit share at the 24.94% aggregate headline rate, reduced by: (i) the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, (ii) the 80% exemption for qualifying IP income, (iii) the notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity, and (iv) unlimited tax-loss carryforward at the corporate partner level where substance is maintained.
